title: The Sky That Learned to Read

features.name: light-page
features.desc-on-touch: The sky holds a moment of text written purely in sunbeam. You read it as you read warmth — through your skin, into your bones. The words dissolve as you understand them.

features.name: word-drift
features.desc-on-touch: Clouds hold syllables before the wind erases them. Each cloudshape reads differently to each reader. The sky is learning that reading is never complete.

features.name: horizon-margin
features.desc-on-touch: The line where sky meets earth has become a binding. You trace it with your eyes as if reading the margin of a book that holds the whole world.

features.name: open-study
features.desc-on-touch: The pages of an enormous book lie open to the sky. No cover, no binding — just text reading itself to the birds and the light and whatever listens.

features.name: wind-reader
features.desc-on-touch: A device of threads and hollows that translates wind-pressure into sequential meaning. The archive learning that reading need not require eyes.

inscription: the pages here taught themselves that sky is the only true paper

file.name: Sky_Marginalia_Light_Refraction_Log.txt
file.note: Daily record of what the sky appears to be saying, collected over a decade. Increasingly difficult to distinguish observation from interpretation. The last entry simply reads: 'the sky is reading too.

reverie.title: REVERIE — reading in high grass
narr: You both lie in the tall grass, eyes on the sky,
tracing shapes in clouds like pages you've each read
a thousand times and still discover anew. She points:
'There — that's the word for arriving just in time.'
You see it dissolve as you look. She laughs. The sky
is patient. It will spell it again for anyone who listens.
